title: Joe Turner's recordings and New Orleans recording studios
summary: Harris says Turner recorded blues, probably for Atlantic, and discusses the local studios, J&M and WDSU.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: If you remember which records you made with him and what label?

Joe, Joe, Joe Blues. The only thing he would make was a blues. He just only made blues numbers like that. But, uh, blues numbers, I couldn't even tell you the name of them. So many of them. Yeah, it's... Anything they have... What were the thought of the album? Atlantic. I think it was Atlantic.
Atlantic. Some of those were out on a long play. I don't remember. I thought they were mostly a New York band or...

No, Joe, Joe would make a section in here. He would make a section here at any time when he comes, if he got anything to offer. Yeah. Because we have studios here, you know. You get anywhere, you stop over in Chicago and make a section. Anywhere you stop.
Where are the studios in here, in this town?
I think it's down on St. Claude. We have one on St. Claude and I think you can record at WDSU studio too.
Yeah, he's got J and M studio. Yes, that's down on St. Claude.
He's down on Governor Nichols or something. Yeah.

Well, that was our boy. We used to go to him for everything. Well, Dave O'Connor is a representative for the Imperial Recording Company and I think they do business together. So every section that he had, we have it down there at the J and M.
